sources.optical_input_sensor: Landsat 8/9 OLI via NASA/USGS HLS L30
sources.optical_derived_quantity: NDVI change on common clear, non-water HLS pixels

sar_provider_qa.basis: Per-product HDF5 QA metadata are retained for both acquisitions. The sidecars do not provide a consolidated PASS/FAIL disposition.
sar_provider_qa.scientific_gate: DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY; QA metadata do not establish temporal registration or validate change interpretation

method.spatial_join: Transform HLS native 30 m pixel polygons and RTC-S1 pixel corner rings into the SAR projected CRS, then intersect polygons and area-weight NDVI change onto SAR cells; no resampling.
method.common_optical_support: Only HLS pixel centers inside the AOI with valid red/NIR/Fmask, no cloud/adjacency/shadow/snow/water flags, and no high-aerosol flag on both dates contribute.
method.association_metric: Pearson correlation between area-weighted NDVI change and signed SAR gamma-zero log-ratio; descriptive only.

coverage_sensitivity.inferential_statistics: NOT_COMPUTED; neighboring cells are spatially dependent and RTC-S1 provider QA is diagnostic

interpretation_limits: The per-cell association is observational and descriptive; it does not demonstrate that vegetation change caused the SAR response.
Only common clear-land pixels contribute, so the result does not represent cloud-, water-, snow-, or high-aerosol-masked areas.
The RTC-S1 pair lacks a consolidated provider QA verdict and remains diagnostic.
NDVI is a vegetation spectral index, not a direct biomass or soil-moisture measurement.
The association is not an independent SAR validation or a calibrated predictive model.
